title: Observationally Informed Adaptive Causal Experimental Design

problem.claim: Randomized controlled trials are the gold standard for causal inference but are scarce.

gap.claim: Observational data is often available but is typically discarded during prospective trial design because of bias concerns.

contributions.claim: Active Residual Learning uses an observational model as an informative but biased prior and estimates residual corrections to debias it.
The R-Design framework operationalizes observationally informed adaptive causal experimental design.
The work characterizes conditional structural efficiency and information-efficiency advantages for residual-focused acquisition.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on synthetic and semi-synthetic benchmarks reportedly show that R-Design significantly outperforms baselines in the informative-but-biased regime.

narrative_sequence.summary: RCTs are scarce despite their central role in causal inference.
Available observational data is generally excluded from prospective trial design because of bias concerns.
Active Residual Learning reframes acquisition around correcting an informative but biased observational model.
R-Design and its theoretical analysis target residual estimation and reduce task-irrelevant acquisition.
Synthetic and semi-synthetic experiments report improved performance over baselines in the intended regime.

source_observation.claim: Observational models may contain useful structural information despite being biased.

interpretation.claim: A biased prior can be useful when the acquisition strategy focuses on estimating its residual errors.

application.claim: In prospective causal experimentation, consider allocating measurements to residual corrections rather than relearning outcomes from scratch.

exception.claim: This lesson is limited to settings where the observational model contains useful structural information and is informative but biased.

source_observation.claim: Parameter-based acquisition can spend budget on nuisance uncertainty unrelated to the downstream causal quantity.

interpretation.claim: Acquisition criteria should target uncertainty relevant to the final causal estimate or policy decision.

application.claim: Use downstream-targeted information-gain criteria when selecting experiments for causal estimation or policy decisions.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this advantage holds beyond the stated informative-but-biased regime.

unknowns: Specific benchmark datasets, baselines, metrics, and quantitative results are not provided.
The assumptions and scope of the theoretical convergence and information-efficiency results are not specified.
The experimental budget, implementation details, and reproducibility materials are not described.
